rows.num: Brought Christianity to the Kingdom of Aksum.

rows.name: Yeshaq
rows.num: An inference from the Kebra Nagast colophon.

rows.name: João Bermudes [pt]
rows.num: Self-proclaimed Ethiopian Orthodox Abuna, and Catholic Patriarch of Ethiopia and Alexandria.

rows.name: Afonso Mendes
rows.num: Catholic Patriarch, supported by Susenyos I and deposed by Fasilides.

rows.name: Atnatewos II
rows.num: Died of wounds received at the Battle of Gura in the Egyptian–Ethiopian War.

rows.name: Qerellos IV
rows.num: First tenure; deposed following the Second Italo-Ethiopian War.

rows.name: Basilios
rows.num: Elevated to Patriarch and Catholicos of All Ethiopia.

rows.name: Paulinus
rows.num: Formerly a monk at St. Andrew's Monastery in Rome; translated to Rochester; canonised.

rows.name: Chad
rows.num: Resigned the see of York; later became bishop of Mercia and Lindsey; canonised.

rows.name: Wilfrid
rows.num: Ejected from York; later became bishop of Selseycanonised.

rows.name: John of Beverley
rows.num: Translated from Hexham; resigned the see; canonised in 1037.

rows.name: Æthelbert
rows.num: Also known as Æthelbeorht, Adalberht, Ælberht, Aelberht, Aldbert or Æthelbert.

rows.name: Wulfhere
rows.num: Fled the Danes in 872, returned in 873.

rows.name: Æthelbald
rows.num: Sometimes known as Æthelbeald, Athelbald, or Ethelbald.

rows.name: Oscytel
rows.num: Also known as Oscytel. Translated from Dorchester.

rows.name: Edwald
rows.num: Also known as Edwaldus or Ethelwold.

rows.name: Oswald
rows.num: Held both the sees of York and Worcester; canonised.

rows.name: Ealdwulf
rows.num: Held both the sees of York and Worcester.

rows.name: Wulfstan
rows.num: Also known as Lupus. Also held the see of Worcester (1002–1016).

rows.name: Ælfric Puttoc
rows.num: Also held the see of Worcester (1040–1041).

rows.name: Ealdred
rows.num: Also known as Aldred. Held the see of Worcester 1046–1061, of Hereford 1056–1060, and of York 1061–1069.

rows.name: Thurstan
rows.num: He was elected in 1114, but was not consecrated until 1119.

rows.name: Waltheof of Melrose
rows.num: Nominated archbishop, but was quashed by King Stephen; later became Abbot of Melrose.

rows.name: Henry de Sully
rows.num: Abbot of Fécamp Abbey. Nominated archbishop, but was quashed by Pope Innocent II.

rows.name: William
rows.num: Deposed by Pope Eugene III; canonised in 1226.

rows.name: Hilary of Chichester
rows.num: Deposed by Pope Eugene III, elected bishop of Chichester.

rows.name: William (FitzHerbert)
rows.num: Restored by Pope Anastasius IV; canonised in 1226.

rows.name: Geoffrey
rows.num: Formerly bishop-elect of Lincoln; elected archbishop in 1189, but was only consecrated in 1191.

rows.name: Simon Langton
rows.num: Elected archbishop of York in June 1215, but was quashed on 20 August 1215 by Pope Innocent III on request from King John; later became archdeacon of Canterbury.

rows.name: Godfrey Ludham
rows.num: Also known as Godfrey Kineton. Formerly Dean of York.

rows.name: William Langton
rows.num: Dean of York (1262–1279); elected archbishop in March 1265, but was quashed in November 1265.

rows.name: Bonaventure
rows.num: Selected as archbishop in November 1265, but never consecrated and resigned the appointment in October 1266.

rows.name: William Zouche
rows.num: Also known as William de la Zouche.

rows.name: Cardinal John of Thoresby
rows.num: Translated from Worcester; created a Cardinal in 1361.

rows.name: Thomas Arundel
rows.num: Translated from Ely; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Walter Skirlaw
rows.num: Bishop of Durham, elected but put aside by King Richard II.

rows.name: Thomas Langley
rows.num: Elected archbishop in August 1405, but was quashed in May 1406.

rows.name: Robert Hallam
rows.num: Nominated archbishop in May 1406 by Pope Innocent VII, but was vetoed by King Henry IV.

rows.name: Philip Morgan
rows.num: Elected archbishop in 1423, but was quashed in 1424.

rows.name: Richard Fleming
rows.num: Conferred as archbishop by Pope Martin V, but was refused by King Henry V, and Fleming resigned the appointment in July 1425.

rows.name: Cardinal John Kemp
rows.num: Translated from London; created a Cardinal in 1439; translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Cardinal Christopher Bainbridge
rows.num: Translated from Durham; created a Cardinal in 1511.

rows.name: Cardinal Thomas Wolsey
rows.num: Translated from Lincoln in 1514; created a Cardinal in 1515; held with Bath and Wells 1518–23, Durham 1523–29 and Winchester 1529–30.

rows.name: Edmund Grindal
rows.num: Translated from London; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: John Williams
rows.num: Translated from Lincoln. Deprived when the English episcopacy was abolished by Parliament. Died 1650.

rows.name: Thomas Herring
rows.num: Translated from Bangor; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Matthew Hutton
rows.num: Translated from Bangor; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Edward Venables-Vernon
rows.num: Translated from Carlisle. Surname changed from Venables-Vernon to Venables-Vernon-Harcourt in 1831.

rows.name: Charles Longley
rows.num: Translated from Durham; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Cosmo Gordon Lang
rows.num: Translated from Stepney; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: William Temple
rows.num: Translated from Manchester; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Michael Ramsey
rows.num: Translated from Durham; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Donald Coggan
rows.num: Translated from Bradford; afterwards translated to Canterbury.

rows.name: Stephen Cottrell
rows.num: Translated from Chelmsford; election confirmed 9 July 2020.
